operation: diagnose and relieve a fetch stall: one failed robots.txt read blocked scoring.dance for a day and starved every other host

symptom.requests_by_hour: 10-08 only in 02:xx; 10-09 only in 14:xx (after a Mac wake at 14:22)
symptom.acquire_ticks: from 2026-10-09T14:54Z every tick ran its 240 s budget with checked=0

diagnosis.tool: py-spy 0.4 record of one acquire tick (230 s, 4,334 samples)
diagnosis.profile: 68% in fairness._eligible/_choices, 45% prepare_event_turns, 40% next_watch; each pass loop iteration re-lists all ~1,443 due choices
diagnosis.guard_reasons: 654 'robots disallow' rows for scoringdance watches (502 since 2026-10-08T02, 81 since 2026-10-09T14)
diagnosis.cause: fetch/robots.py caches the robots answer for one day whatever its status; a transport failure (599) or 5xx means disallow-all (correct), so scoring.dance stayed blocked for 24 h; acquire then picked each due scoring.dance watch first, skipped it as robots-disallowed, and re-ran the whole candidate selection per skip (about 0.4 s), so the 4-minute budget ended before any registry page; the same happened from about 2026-10-08T02Z

relief.change: hosts.robots_fetched_at for scoring.dance 2026-10-09T14:23:15.930233Z -> 2026-10-08T00:00:00Z (one row, one field), so the worker re-reads robots.txt through its own gate

fix: queued: a failed robots read retries after a short backoff instead of a day, and acquire skips a robots-blocked host once per pass instead of per watch (code change with tests, deployed with contract 5 after a check)
